comparisons.finding: Clear input–Expand–Ask sequence. Helper copy adds height; at 500px/200%, Expand and Ask require page scrolling. Expanded editor provides substantially more writing space with visible Done/Cancel controls.

Strongest direct writing composition: generous input and visible Ask in every supplied configuration. At 500px/200%, heading and duplicate question labels leave only about two visible input lines; reclaiming that space would improve editing.

Prompt rows compete with the populated input. At 500px/200%, neither input nor Ask appears initially; both are reachable in the bottom capture. Expanded editor is as strong visually as A, but the entry composition creates unnecessary scrolling.

Strongest explanation-first reading order. Section headings, answer labels and dividers distinguish content without extra controls. At 200%, the document grows substantially, but supplied bottom views show readable assumptions and sources.

Selector and focused text are visually clean, including at 200%. Starting with absent assumptions gives little explanatory value and conceals the other section names until the selector is opened. Selection behavior is not demonstrated.

Disclosure rows expose available sections more clearly than B's closed selector and remain visible at 200%. However, the largest content block describes missing assumptions while the useful explanation is collapsed. Expanded reading states are absent.

Full portrait best communicates the orb, branding and complete visual composition. Its embedded text does not enlarge with surrounding text; at 200%, Download requires scrolling. No separate enlarged transcript is shown.

Best balance of visual identity, immediately visible Download and scalable forecast/qualifier text. Thumbnail establishes the portrait's appearance without dominating. At 200%, the button wraps cleanly; the full-image route needs a short scroll and its result is unshown.

Most straightforward enlarged-text composition: forecast, qualifier, full-width Download and disclosure remain visible at 200%. Hiding the entire portrait weakens understanding of the visual artifact being shared; the expanded preview is unshown.

reason: B makes writing and submission most direct across the constrained views. A presents the explanation and supporting sections in a coherent reading order. B combines sharing identity, readable content and action reachability. No composition demonstrates the authorized threshold across every dimension and component.
limitations: Provisional visual assessment of supplied images and stated prototype checks only; no source, other reviews or runtime inspection.
Component observations cover visible inputs, buttons, editor overlay, prompts, headings, selector, disclosures and portrait. They do not establish component interaction performance.
Feedback scores are null: the stated prototype draft-preservation exercise does not establish comprehensive feedback, recovery or production persistence.
Accessibility scores assess visible enlargement and layout only. Keyboard access, focus behavior, screen readers, measured contrast, target sizes and reduced motion remain unverified.
Exports, navigation, disclosure results and evidence provenance are not proven. The unchanged exported portrait is not graded as a different artifact across variants.
No demonstrated hard-gate failure: offscreen actions appear in supplied bottom views. This does not establish all interaction paths or native behavior.
No full/native 9–10 certification or loop acceptance is supported; physical iPhone and assistive-technology validation remain outstanding.
